correctness.rationale: Write high-count h_i, value rL+(H−L)h_i. For target with a low good, removing low is strongest EFX inequality (H−L)(h_j−h_i)≤L; for all-high target, inequality (H−L)(r−h_i)≤H. When H≤2L, evenly spaced high counts h_i differing by ≤1 meet both; when H>2L, any not-full bundle must share the minimum high count a since integer positive differences violate first inequality. If full bundle coexists with mixed, (r−a)(H−L)≤H=(H−L)+L and H−L>L forces r−a=1; so either q multiple n or q>(r−1)n. Equal-count and top-layer constructions prove converse. Exact labelled goods multinomial counts follow by partitioning distinct high and low items into fixed h_i profiles, including q=nr. Independently enumerated all high-count vectors in 12 (n,r,H,L) small parameter tuples and verified feasibility iff. For iid high goods B_n~Bin(nr,p), exact event B_n>n(r−1) or B_n=jn for j≤r−1 gives CLT critical p*=(r−1)/r with scale β r^(3/2)/sqrt(r−1), Chernoff exponential tails, resonant local CLT n^-1/2 at j/r (1≤j≤r−2). At p=p* limit 1/2. Identical valuation total sum fixed makes every allocation fPO trivially, but does not prove EFX. These rigorous universal statements do not rely on finite checks.
residual_risks: Requires n>=2, r>=1, strictly positive L and H>L, iid item high probability and fixed r for CLT.
No inference for agents with heterogeneous valuations or zero-value goods.
